clue.text: Shrubs give credit for what belongs to a witch

parts.note: broom is a yellow-flowered shrub, so shrubs are brooms
to tick is to let someone buy on tick, that is, on credit

explanation.surface: A gardener credits shrubs with some witchy property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for 'on credit', so to give credit is to tick.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch traditionally flies on a besom, the stick-and-twigs sweeping brush.

clue.text: Sound made by lazy person on the piano

parts.note: a bum is an idle loafer
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A layabout clunks away at the piano keys.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the piano's P below BUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A thud or knock is a dull sound, the noise of something hitting.

clue.text: Seat which will do for Empire

explanation.surface: Someone says a certain seat will serve as an empire.
explanation.definitionFit: A low cushioned footstool or couch is named after the Turkish empire that ruled from Constantinople.

clue.text: Material minds are disorganised and govern badly

indicators.note: letters that are disorganised are thrown into disorder and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Materialistic minds are muddled and lead to poor government.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer is to manage or govern; the prefix meaning badly makes it poor government.

clue.text: Staying power which ensures a premier's headquarters takes precedence over a place to live

indicators.note: taking precedence means coming first, so this piece leads the ones after it

parts.note: the British prime minister lives and works at No. 10 Downing Street
a city is a place where people live

explanation.surface: A prime minister's office has priority over housing, showing persistence.
explanation.walkthrough: TEN is No. 10 Downing Street, the British prime minister's official residence and office.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggedness, the quality of holding on and not giving up, is staying power.

clue.text: Caught what may be hot for witches

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
an oven is something that may be hot

explanation.surface: Someone is caught by something hot, suggesting witch-burning.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of thirteen witches is the traditional collective noun for them.

clue.text: City is in a go-slow area

indicators.note: the city is said to be in the words, so it lies within them

explanation.surface: A city sits in an area hit by a go-slow work protest.
explanation.walkthrough: A go-slow is a British form of industrial action in which workers deliberately slow down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian capital is a city.

clue.text: Creature with under-water ear

parts.note: under water is down in the seas, so the hyphenated word stands for seas
lug is informal British for an ear

explanation.surface: A creature has an ear that works underwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lug' (or lughole) is British slang for an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell-less marine mollusc is a living creature.

clue.text: Obscure deliveries were all accurately bowled

parts.note: an over is a set of six deliveries in cricket
no wides, W being the cricket scorer's mark for a wide

explanation.surface: Cricket report: deliveries were obscure, yet all bowled on target.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach; accurate bowling gives none, so the overs HAD O (nil) W (wides).
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in the shade, making it less noticeable, is to obscure it.

clue.text: Encountered a beginner in tin, possibly

parts.note: to have met someone is to have encountered them
L is a learner, from the L-plate a learner driver displays

explanation.surface: Meeting a novice in a tin, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin is an example of an element of that class, so the 'possibly' marks it as one instance.

clue.text: Perhaps I can vote one into the collection of beginners

indicators.note: one is put into the rearranged letters
perhaps says the letters may be some other arrangement, so they are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they can vote one person into a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges I CAN VOTE, and 'into' then puts I (one) inside those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A noviciate is the period or body of novices in a religious order, those just beginning.

clue.text: Premier joiners?

parts.note: read as the top tradesmen in woodwork, but also prime ministers who form a government's senior group

explanation.surface: A question about the best carpenters around.
explanation.walkthrough: Joiners are woodworkers who make furniture; a premier (prime minister) also forms a cabinet, a government's top team.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture craftsmen build cupboards, while a prime minister assembles a government's senior ministers.

clue.text: Hospital dances? They provide exercise

parts.note: a hospital is the world of medicine, the place it is practised
balls are formal dances

explanation.surface: Dances held at a hospital, offered as a form of exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy balls thrown and caught in gym training are used for exercise.

clue.text: Impractical, and such a person makes a plan appear wrecked

definitions.text: Impractical, and such a person makes a plan appear wrecked

parts.words: Impractical, and such a person makes a plan appear wrecked
parts.note: a person given to lofty, unrealistic aims is built from a word for a plan followed by what a wrecked ship appears to do as it leans

explanation.surface: An unrealistic dreamer whose schemes look shipwrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue opens with a plain definition, then hints at the noun inside the answer: a plan (IDEA) plus what a wrecked ship does, LIST (lean over).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose aims are noble but unrealistic is impractical.

clue.text: They often stop at work

parts.note: reads as people pausing on the job, but here to stop is to fill a cavity in a tooth

explanation.surface: Workers who keep pausing on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'stop' a tooth is an old term for filling it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooth doctors fill (stop) cavities as part of their daily work.

clue.text: Problem for an English graduate about putting a drink back

indicators.note: about means the graduate's letters go round the next piece

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: putting the drink back means writing its letters in reverse order

parts.note: gin is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: An English graduate has trouble with a drink being returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns GIN into NIG, which E and MA wrap round ('about').
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle or mystery that is hard to understand is a problem.

clue.text: Edition which makes Virginia city strange

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian city
rum is British informal for odd or strange

explanation.surface: An edition that makes a Virginian city seem odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' is old-fashioned British slang for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A variorum is an edition of a text with notes by various scholars.

clue.text: Although dexterous, I enter the rubbish after time

indicators.note: after places the rubbish piece behind the time piece

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the era of time we count dates in

indicators.note: I enter means the letter goes inside the word for rubbish

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Despite being skilful, someone wanders into the garbage after hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Being skilful and nimble with the hands is being dexterous.

clue.text: If it lost a point the animal would look more embarrassed

indicators.note: if the answer lost a letter it would become the comparative word, so that letter is added to it

parts.note: someone more embarrassed is redder in the face
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An animal that blushes harder if it loses a point.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: take E (a compass point) out of the answer and you get REDDER, so REDDER with E put in gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A large deer of Europe and Asia is an animal.

clue.text: Censor holds culture back for singer

indicators.note: holds means the censor's name contains the next piece

parts.note: Cato the Elder held the Roman office of censor

indicators.note: back means the word for culture is written backwards

parts.note: the arts are culture

explanation.surface: A censor keeps culture back from a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns ARTS into STRA, which CATO holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated male singer kept a soprano or alto voice.

clue.text: Truly one enters thanks for a handicap

parts.note: amen means 'so be it', truly

indicators.note: one enters means the letter goes inside the word for thanks

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grateful 'truly' becomes a disability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ta' is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe mental deficiency from birth is an old medical term for a disability.

clue.text: Vague but fashionable as in an inhabitant about to offer discouragement

indicators.note: the fashionable word goes in the inhabitant word
about means the inhabitant word goes round the discouraging word

parts.note: an inmate is an inhabitant of an institution
to deter is to discourage
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: An inhabitant about to discourage, vague but trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions: INMATE goes 'about' DETER (IN-DETER-MATE), then IN (fashionable) goes in between M and ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Not fixed or clearly decided means vague.

clue.text: Red may be seen in front but cross over

indicators.note: the colour can be seen inside the words, meaning its letters lie within them

explanation.surface: Red may show at the front of a cross.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosso is the Italian for red.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for red, used in English for red wine (vino rosso).

clue.text: The goddess shows the gentleman up after one

indicators.note: after puts the gentleman piece behind the one piece

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: sir is a form of address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A goddess shows a man up after one.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is the Greek goddess of the rainbow.

clue.text: Thinker who is the one who rebels about nothing

indicators.note: about means the earlier words go round the nought

parts.note: taken as written
a riser rises up in rebellion
O is the figure nought, nothing

explanation.surface: A thinker who rebels over nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: One who forms theories is a thinker.

clue.text: Listener includes note for consumer

indicators.note: includes means the listener word contains the note

parts.note: the ear is the organ of listening
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A listener takes in a note for a consumer.
explanation.definitionFit: One who eats food is a consumer of it.

clue.text: Ear or foot growth

explanation.surface: A choice between an ear and a growth on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A grain head is an ear of cereal; a hard painful lump of skin on a toe is a foot growth.

clue.text: Russian officials who keep company with a young lady in a kind of bar

indicators.note: in means the young lady goes inside the bar

parts.note: a Mars bar is a chocolate bar
miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Soviet officials keep company with a young woman in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mars bar is a chocolate bar, familiar in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Soviet heads of government departments were people's commissars, officials.
